title: ER stress-induced modulation of neural activity and seizure susceptibility is impaired in a fragile X syndrome mouse model.
authors: Liu, Dai-Chi; Lee, Kwan Young; Lizarazo, Simon; Cook, Jessie K; Tsai, Nien-Pei
one_liner_zh: 该文研究脆性X综合征小鼠模型中ER应激对神经活动与癫痫易感性的调控，不涉及蛋白质-DNA互作、结合位点预测或AI/物理模拟方法，与本课题无关。
abstract: Imbalanced neuronal excitability homeostasis is commonly observed in patients with fragile X syndrome (FXS) and the animal model of FXS, the Fmr1 KO. While alterations of neuronal intrinsic excitability and synaptic activity at the steady state in FXS have been suggested to contribute to such a deficit and ultimately the increased susceptibility to seizures in FXS, it remains largely unclear whether and how the homeostatic response of neuronal excitability following extrinsic challenges is disrupted in FXS. Our previous work has shown that the acute response following induction of endoplasmic reticulum (ER) stress can reduce neural activity and seizure susceptibility. Because many signaling pathways associated with ER stress response are mediated by Fmr1, we asked whether acute ER stress-induced reduction of neural activity and seizure susceptibility are altered in FXS. Our results first revealed that acute ER stress can trigger a protein synthesis-dependent prevention of neural network synchronization in vitro and a reduction of susceptibility to kainic acid-induced seizures in vivo in wild-type but not in Fmr1 KO mice. Mechanistically, we found that acute ER stress-induced activation of murine double minute-2 (Mdm2), ubiquitination of p53, and the subsequent transient protein synthesis are all impaired in Fmr1 KO neurons. Employing a p53 inhibitor, Pifithrin-alpha, to mimic p53 inactivation, we were able to blunt the increase in neural network synchronization and reduce the seizure susceptibility in Fmr1 KO mice following ER stress induction. In summary, our data revealed a novel cellular defect in Fmr1 KO mice and suggest that an impaired response to common extrinsic challenges may contribute to imbalanced neuronal excitability homeostasis in FXS.
abstract_zh: 在脆性X综合征（FXS）患者及其动物模型Fmr1 KO中，常观察到神经元兴奋性稳态失衡。尽管已有研究表明，FXS中稳态下的神经元固有兴奋性和突触活性的改变可能促成这种缺陷，并最终导致FXS对癫痫发作的易感性增加，但关于FXS中神经元兴奋性在外部挑战后的稳态反应是否及如何被破坏，仍 largely 不清楚。我们先前的工作表明，诱导内质网（ER）应激后的急性反应可降低神经活动和癫痫易感性。由于许多与ER应激反应相关的信号通路由Fmr1介导，我们探究了急性ER应激诱导的神经活动降低和癫痫易感性变化是否在FXS中发生改变。我们的结果首先揭示，急性ER应激可在体外触发一种依赖蛋白质合成的神经网络同步化抑制，并在体内降低野生型小鼠对海人酸诱导癫痫发作的易感性，但在Fmr1 KO小鼠中无此效应。机制上，我们发现急性ER应激诱导的鼠双微体2（Mdm2）激活、p53泛素化及随后的瞬时蛋白质合成在Fmr1 KO神经元中均受损。使用p53抑制剂Pifithrin-alpha模拟p53失活，我们能够减弱Fmr1 KO小鼠在ER应激诱导后神经网络同步化的增加，并降低其癫痫易感性。总之，我们的数据揭示了Fmr1 KO小鼠中一种新的细胞缺陷，并提示对外部常见挑战的受损反应可能促成FXS中神经元兴奋性稳态失衡。
